data.short_meaning: Lady of the house of the Lord
data.long_meaning: Derived from 'Lora' meaning 'maiden' and 'dana' meaning 'of the Lord'. This name signifies a woman who is devoted to God and is the mistress of her household. The name Loredana carries the meaning “Lady of the house of the Lord” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Loredana usually hope their child will grow to embody lady of the house of the lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A woman who embodies the divine presence in her home.
data.etymology: Loredana belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lady of the house of the Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Loredana total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_latin.name: Loredana
in_latin.meaning: Feminine form of Loredano, derived from Loro and Danna
in_latin.long_meaning: Feminine form of Loredano, derived from Loro, meaning 'glory of the people,' and Danna, meaning 'judged.' Often associated with the Latin word 'laudare,' meaning 'to praise,' and 'dignitas,' meaning 'dignity.'

in_english.name: Loredana
in_english.meaning: Feminine form of Loredano, derived from glory and judged
in_english.long_meaning: Feminine form of Loredano, derived from Loro, meaning 'glory of the people,' and Danna, meaning 'judged.' Often associated with the Latin word 'laudare,' meaning 'to praise,' and 'dignitas,' meaning 'dignity.' Etymologically linked to the Hebrew words 'kavod,' meaning 'glory,' and 'dina,' meaning 'judged.' In Christian tradition, Loredana is seen as a symbol of divine glory and dignity, reflecting the character of God as the ultimate judge and rewarder of the faithful.

data.cultural_impact: The name Loredana might have originated in Italy, and its popularity is still prevalent among Italian communities. Loredana is a gentle, feminine name, often associated with the Italian Renaissance, when the Catholic Church had a significant impact on Italian culture and society.
data.spiritual_significance: Loredana's name invokes a deep sense of devotion and faith. Loredana is a reminder of the power and presence of God in a woman's life. The name suggests a woman who is connected to her spiritual side, and her faith guides her actions and decisions. Loredana is a beacon of grace and strength, and her name inspires her to live a virtuous life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Loredana, derived from 'Loretta' meaning 'lady' or 'maiden', carries the deeper meaning of a dedicated and virtuous woman. She is a beacon of grace and purity, embodying the spirit of devotion and loyalty to God. Her name is a reminder to uphold feminine virtues and maintain a strong connection with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Loredana, a beautiful Venetian woman, was the lover of the powerful poet Petrarch in the 14th century. She was the idealized image of love and beauty in his sonnets.

Loredana, a noblewoman from Ragusa, Dalmatia, was the wife of Pope Alexander VI in the late 15th century. Her influence helped secure the papal throne for her husband and protected the interests of her hometown.
